articles.title: First data center bill clears House as both parties scramble for answers on affordability
articles.summary: The Ratepayer Protection Act passed the House with bipartisan support, aiming to stop data center energy costs from raising electric bills for families.
articles.body: The U.S. House of Representatives on Wednesday passed the Ratepayer Protection Act (RPA), a bill that looks to shield communities from higher energy electricity and grid infrastructure costs associated with data center development. The bill, which succeeded with broad bipartisan support in a 417-3 vote, is likely one of the last pieces of legislation lawmakers will consider until after the Nov. 3 midterm elections. It also puts a spotlight on the data center issue, which has garnered attention as a proxy for affordability, energy and regulatory debates. It marks the first data center-related bill passed in the 119th Congress. WHO PAYS FOR US POWER BOOM? BLUE, RED STATES OFFER STARKLY DIFFERENT WAYS TO LOWER UTILITY BILLS AMID AI SURGE In its current form, the bill does not seek to ban data centers, set limitations on their expansion or even set regulatory guidelines for them. Instead, it amends existing energy law, the Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act (PURPA), so states must consider a federal standard. Large data centers that consume 100 megawatts or more would pay the full extra cost of the generation, transmission and distribution upgrades built to serve them. Companies would also be required to make financial assurances in the event a project is canceled or moved to prevent communities from being left holding the bill. Its sponsor, Rep. Gabe Evans, R-Colo., framed it as a needed step toward keeping data center energy costs from spilling over to local communities. "As America races to lead the world in AI, we must build the energy infrastructure needed to support this innovation and stay ahead of competitors like communist China," Evans said in a statement earlier this year. "But Colorado families, farmers and small businesses should not be forced to cover the costs of new power generation driven by these developments. The Ratepayer Protection Act is a bipartisan, commonsense solution that protects everyday Americans and ensures our nation can continue to win the AI race." The bill’s Democratic co-sponsor, Rep. Kathy Castor, D-Fla., echoed Evans’ thinking. AMERICA NEEDS AI TO SURVIVE. WORKING FAMILIES ALSO NEED TO SURVIVE IT "My neighbors across Florida are grappling with skyrocketing electric bills. Ratepayers should not have to subsidize wealthy corporations’ growing energy demands, especially from AI data centers," Castor said. In recent months, candidates from both sides of the aisle have carefully framed their thinking about data centers. Democrats, in particular, have linked the issue to affordability. Such is the case for Roy Cooper, former governor of North Carolina, who is now waging a bid for the seat of retiring Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C. Cooper, once having celebrated data center expansion as an avenue for job growth in the Tar Heel State, has since qualified his support. "Roy believes local communities must have the final say on new projects coming to their area, which includes local moratoriums, and data centers must pay for all of the energy they use without passing on any of their costs to consumers," a spokesperson for Cooper’s campaign said in a statement to Fox News Digital earlier this month. Republicans have also navigated the political noise around data centers with care. Cooper’s opponent, former Republican National Committee Chairman Michael Whatley, also stressed allowing local communities decide for themselves about whether data center expansion is right for them. MAGA BEGINS TO CRACK AS 2026 GOP ROSTER BACKS AWAY FROM TRUMP'S TECH VISION "Michael Whatley's standard is simple: Data centers pay their own way, families pay nothing and communities decide. That means Big Tech builds or buys every megawatt it needs and covers every dime of the grid upgrades to deliver it, with zero costs shifted onto residential ratepayers. It means no special subsidies and no sweetheart deals cut over the heads of taxpayers," Whatley’s campaign said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Having cleared the House, the data center bill passed Wednesday heads to the Senate, where its fate is uncertain.

articles.title: Skid Row forgeries, illegal votes and a mayoral candidate: Election fraud cases pile up nationwide
articles.summary: Noncitizen voting and fraudulent voter registration cases were announced across several states this week, adding to DOJ's growing election fraud prosecutions from recent weeks.
articles.body: The Trump administration continues to crack down on voter fraud cases, including a noncitizen who allegedly voted in a mayoral race he was fraudulently registered for and a noncitizen arrested for allegedly lying about her citizenship to vote in federal elections. These allegations span a slate of federal election-related cases highlighted by the Justice Department in recent days, adding to a series of prosecutions targeting noncitizen voting, fraudulent voter registrations and other alleged election-related crimes. The DOJ's latest announcements involve California, Kansas, Louisiana, Texas and Massachusetts, while federal prosecutors have brought a number of other cases across the country in recent weeks amid the Trump administration's broader efforts to bolster election security ahead of the midterms. The White House pointed to the new cases that continue to pile up as evidence supporting the administration's crackdown. DEMOCRAT NEW JERSEY GOVERNOR SAYS THOUSANDS OF NONCITIZENS DISCOVERED ON VOTER ROLLS, PURGED "Despite extreme Democrats and the media claiming it never happens, the evidence of noncitizens registering and voting in our elections continues to pile up," White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis told Fox News Digital. "Any noncitizens found registering and voting in our elections will be arrested and held accountable. Only Americans should be electing American leaders." The more than a dozen defendants charged in cases announced this week face allegations ranging from illegal voting and false claims of U.S. citizenship to fraudulent voter registration and identity fraud. U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche warned that individuals "gaming the election system, voting illegally or committing voter fraud" will face prosecution, while federal prosecutors in Texas said their seven cases "send a clear message" that laws barring noncitizens from voting will be enforced. Among the defendants were Louisiana mayoral candidate Bridget Johnson, who prosecutors allege fraudulently registered Jamaican noncitizen Michael Wedderburn before he voted in the 2024 federal election and the same mayoral race in which Johnson was a candidate. Johnson allegedly electronically submitted a Louisiana voter registration application in Wedderburn's name on July 14, 2024, falsely stating that he was a U.S. citizen, according to court documents. ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT LEARNS FATE AFTER USING STOLEN IDENTITY TO VOTE IN US ELECTIONS FOR DECADES Johnson was charged with fraudulent voter registration and voting by an alien, while Wedderburn was charged with voting by an alien. If convicted, Johnson faces up to five years in prison, while Wedderburn faces up to one year, along with potential financial penalties, according to federal prosecutors. Other cases announced this week included allegations against three people in California accused in an alleged scheme that used stolen identities of registered voters to manufacture signatures on ballot initiative petitions. California frequently uses ballot initiatives to put major policy questions directly before voters, with citizen-backed measures capable of changing state law or amending the state constitution. Recent initiatives have included Proposition 36, which increased penalties for certain drug and theft crimes, and measures dealing with the minimum wage and rent control. Prosecutors allege James Brass and Courtney Price went to Los Angeles' Skid Row, where they handed people stolen identities belonging to registered California voters and paid them to copy those voters' personal information onto ballot petitions and forge their signatures. Brass and a third defendant, Jateisha Herron, then allegedly falsely certified that they had personally witnessed the registered voters sign the petitions. Brass allegedly received about $41,600 from coordinators working with a petition-management company helping collect signatures, according to prosecutors. EX-NEW JERSEY MAYOR, HER HUSBAND CHARGED FOR USING FAKE BALLOT SIGNATURES AFTER SHE PLEADED GUILTY TO DUI The case is the second election-related federal prosecution announced this year involving alleged payments to people on Skid Row. In May, federal prosecutors charged a longtime ballot initiative signature collector with paying individuals, including homeless people living on Skid Row, to register to vote. In Kansas, prosecutors charged 24-year-old Peruvian national and U.S. permanent resident Mariana Alexandra Dewey with falsely claiming U.S. citizenship, fraudulent election conduct and voting as an alien in a federal election after arresting her earlier this month. In Massachusetts, federal prosecutors announced a case this week against Nigerian national Gladys Adaeze Okafor, who allegedly claimed to be a U.S. citizen while registering to vote before casting ballots in multiple federal elections. A handful of cases were announced by federal prosecutors in Texas this week as well, including multiple cases where individuals registered to vote illegally when applying for a Texas driver's license. On the same day those defendants were indicted, a Mexican national was also sentenced to 36 months in federal prison for aggravated identity theft, false statements of citizenship, and illegal voting by an alien, according to federal officials. INSIDE HOUSE REPUBLICANS' PLAN TO END RUN DEM OPPOSITION AND PASS TRUMP-BACKED VOTER ID The cases add to the growing list of federal election-related cases brought in the past few weeks on top of other prosecutions earlier this year involving noncitizens accused of illegally registering or voting in U.S. elections. Less than two weeks ago, the Justice Department charged five people in Pennsylvania, New Jersey and Wisconsin in cases involving alleged illegal voting or fraudulent registration tied to the 2022 or 2024 elections. The DOJ separately charged an Indian national in Minnesota last week with falsely claiming U.S. citizenship in order to vote in the 2024 general election. Despite the mounting prosecutions, the Trump administration also faced a setback this week in its efforts to boost election security. The Supreme Court ruled Monday that the U.S. Postal Service (USPS) could not implement the president's stricter mail ballot requirements for the 2026 elections, leaving a lower court's nationwide injunction in place. The blocked rules would have required states to use specially designed mail ballot envelopes with unique voter barcodes, submit envelope designs to USPS for review and provide it with information about intended ballot recipients. The ruling, however, did not block a separate part of Trump's March executive order directing the federal government to create citizenship lists for states to use in checking their voter rolls. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Conservative Justice Brett Kavanaugh, who was appointed by Trump, agreed the rules should not take effect for this year's elections, writing that state and local officials did not have sufficient time to reasonably implement them. Nonetheless, Kavanaugh said there was "at least a fair prospect" that the Postal Service ultimately has the statutory authority to impose the requirements. Justices Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas dissented. Trump blasted the decision Tuesday as another "bad decision" from the Supreme Court and praised Alito and Thomas as "legends," while arguing the ruling would make cheating through mail ballots easier.

articles.title: Lawmakers say they are standing at the gates against 'Trojan horses' promoting malign foreign interests
articles.summary: House Foreign Affairs Committee members allege CodePink and other groups serve as "Trojan horses" for foreign influence, calling for transparency and FARA disclosure.
articles.body: WASHINGTON, D.C. — In a series of exclusive interviews with Fox News Digital, lawmakers on the House Foreign Affairs Committee sounded the alarm on a sprawling network of "Trojan horse" activists, nonprofits and social media influencers allegedly amplifying the hostile messages of foreign adversaries straight through the open gates of American democracy. The warning came into sharp focus Tuesday when CodePink co-founder Medea Benjamin and two fellow activists walked into House Rayburn 2172 for a hearing on covert foreign influence operations, then strategically positioned themselves behind witnesses in T-shirts supporting the Islamic Republic of Iran and the Communist Party of Cuba. About 30 minutes into the hearing, South and Central Asia Subcommittee Chairman Bill Huizenga, R-Mich., stopped the hearing and had Capitol Police escort them out. LAWMAKERS THROW OUT 'TROJAN HORSE' ACTIVISTS THEY SAY ARE ENGAGED IN AMERICAN SUBVERSION "They're coming in, trying to look like one thing, but we know that once they're inside the gates that those doors are going to spring open, and there's a whole other motivation for what they're trying to do," Huizenga told Fox News Digital. At the center of the controversy is communist tech tycoon Neville Roy Singham, who married CodePink co-founder Jodie Evans in a tropical wedding in Jamaica in 2017, soon after funneling $285 million to six pro-China, pro-communist, anti-American nonprofits in the U.S., including CodePink, according to a Fox News Digital investigation. Lawmakers say the answer is transparency and following the money and exposing who finances the alleged "Trojan horse." In their series of interviews, Huizenga and other committee members explained how the modern "Trojan horse" isn't made of wood but rather a network of activists, nonprofits, social media influencers and other ostensibly American voices that foreign governments and foreign-linked actors can allegedly fund, amplify or exploit to carry their messages through the open gates of American democracy. "They're coming in, trying to look like one thing, but we know that once they're inside the gates that those doors are going to spring open and there's a whole other motivation for what they're trying to do," Huizenga told Fox News Digital. At the hearing, devoted to "Trojan Horses: Covert Foreign Malign Influence Operations in America," lawmakers expressed concern about how the Communist Party of China, Russia, the Islamic Republic of Iran and the Communist Party of Cuba spread their propaganda and influence in the U.S. The phrase "Trojan horse" comes from the ancient Greek story of soldiers concealed inside a wooden horse presented to the city of Troy. Once the horse was taken behind the city's fortified walls, the soldiers emerged and opened the gates, destroying Troy. Huizenga stressed that Americans can hold sincere beliefs while also having those messages funded or amplified by foreign actors without necessarily knowing it. He argued that the answer to foreign influence is exposing the origins of the messaging through transparency and robust debate. Rep. Huizenga: 'It's really about theatrics' Inside the hearing room, as Fox News Digital reported, Benjamin and her fellow CodePink activists offered a vivid illustration of the debate over how political messages are created and amplified. They sat directly behind the witnesses, placing their T-shirts in the sight line of the official committee cameras. Benjamin then turned toward a television monitor on the side of the hearing room displaying the official video feed. She pulled out her phone, zoomed in on the image of herself and a fellow activist appearing behind the witnesses and took photo after photo of the screen. HOUSE PANEL PROBES FOREIGN ‘TROJAN HORSES’ AS SINGHAM SCRUTINY WIDENS Huizenga said he viewed the episode as political theater designed for an audience beyond the committee room. "This isn't about discourse. This is about disruption," Huizenga told Fox News Digital. "It's all planned out. You see people in the crowd filming with their phones, getting ready. You knew something was going to happen because, all of a sudden, the phones would come out. "It's really about theatrics," he added, arguing that confrontations can subsequently be circulated on social media to attract attention, donations and volunteers. The episode captured the central tension running through the hearing: How does the United States expose genuine covert foreign influence without treating protected American political speech as foreign subversion? "Transparency. Transparency is the watchword," Huizenga told Fox News Digital. "We really need to make sure that people know not only the why, but the who is behind all this." Rep. Baumgartner: 'We need to know who's behind it' Rep. Michael Baumgartner, R-Wash., told Fox News Digital that America's open political system creates opportunities for foreign governments to try to influence legitimate domestic debates through social media, universities and other institutions. "The American people need transparency and need to understand what is going on in these public policy discussions and whether it's podcast hosts, certain actors on social media or things going on our college campuses," Baumgartner said. "We need to know who's behind it and what their motivations are." Baumgartner pointed to "clear transparency on this issue" as a solution, adding that if evidence showed organizations were acting on behalf of foreign governments without complying with applicable disclosure laws, the matter could potentially be referred to the Justice Department, which oversees the Foreign Agent Registration Act, or FARA. The law requires that people and organizations acting on behalf of foreign interests register with the Justice Department. Rep. Randy Fine: Trojan horses ‘poison people’s minds’ Other lawmakers said the modern Trojan horse doesn't necessarily have to walk physically through the doors of Congress, but rather arrive via social media. Rep. Randy Fine, R-Fla., described social media, influencers and protests as potential channels through which foreign governments influence American political debate. He said "it's a real issue, whether it's on social media, influencers, protests, these things are all designed to destabilize our country." Fine characterized what experts call "cognitive warfare" as "using our information platforms to try to poison people's minds and to create division from within." Rep. Darrell Issa: ‘It’s a network’ Rep. Darrell Issa, R-Calif., focused on another battlefield: artificial intelligence. "Trojan horses are things like the announcement that we should slow down on AI," Issa told Fox News Digital, arguing that foreign adversaries can benefit when American political pressure slows U.S. technological development. "We are in a war in which the other side uses all the clandestine tools," Issa said. "They use their, quite frankly, their social media to our detriment." Huizenga similarly argued that Americans should view the organizations under examination not individually but as a network. "It's a network. It's not independent organizations or even people," he said. "You will see some of the same people at different organizations, rallies, or protests." ‘Origins aren’t organic’ At the center of much of the hearing were findings from a Fox News Digital investigation into Neville Roy Singham, an American-born communist tech tycoon who lives in Shanghai and has pumped $285 million into six nonprofits, including CodePink, the People's Forum and other groups examined during the hearing. Huizenga alleged in his official opening remarks that Singham uses his wealth and relationships in China to support organizations that promote communist ideology and destabilize American society. He explicitly described Singham, CodePink and a growing network of pro-communist, pro-China groups as "Trojan horses." ‘TROJAN HORSES’ IN AMERICA: CONGRESS PROBES INFLUENCE NETWORKS TIED TO CHINA, IRAN AND CUBA Singham and CodePink have denied taking direction from the Chinese government. Singham has said his activities reflect his own political beliefs, while Benjamin has said CodePink doesn't receive money from the Chinese Communist Party. As Fox News Digital reported in June, the Justice Department and the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of New York have convened a grand jury investigation into alleged money laundering, bank fraud and wire fraud by Singham and the organizations he has funded. No criminal charges have been filed against Singham or CodePink with respect to those allegations. Huizenga argued that the funding relationships deserve scrutiny. "Oftentimes, it's frankly the origins aren't organic, or if there is a part of it being organic, this is getting fed by outside organizations, oftentimes even outside countries," Huizenga alleged. ‘Transparency is the watchword’ Being escorted through the committee room doors didn't end CodePink's political theater. Outside the hearing room, Benjamin positioned herself beside the House Foreign Affairs Committee placard and began recording another video, pulling out a comb first to straighten her hair. When Rep. Fine emerged from the hearing, Benjamin followed him down the hallway firing questions as another member of her team recorded the encounter. After Fine disappeared into an office, Benjamin returned to the committee entrance, straightened her hair with a comb and resumed recording. HOUSE COMMITTEE PASSES FOREIGN FUNDING TRANSPARENCY ACT TO EXPOSE FOREIGN DONATIONS TO NONPROFITS About two hours after Capitol Police escorted the activists from the hearing, CodePink posted a carefully edited video of the day's confrontation on social media, where activists in the broader network began sharing it. The physical protest was over, but the images it produced were just beginning to travel. That sequence was precisely why lawmakers said Americans should look beyond the spectacle to who finances and amplifies political messaging. "This is theater for many of these people," Huizenga said. He said he wanted Americans, through "transparency and disclosure," to understand "not just the what they are doing, but the who is financing them." The lawmakers gathered to investigate modern "Trojan horses" said the lesson of the ancient story wasn't simply to keep the horse outside the gates but also to understand what — and who — might be inside. "Transparency. Transparency is the watchword," Huizenga said. Lawmakers say 'transparency and disclosure' are the best defense against influence campaigns exploiting America's democracy. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Fox News Digital's Reagan Schroeder and Brooke Curto contributed to this report.

articles.title: Top Democrat Gregory Meeks opposes US sale of heavy bombs to Israel
articles.summary: But the objection is not enough to stop the sale - the Trump administration can still press ahead.
articles.body:
The top Democrat on a congressional committee that reviews weapons deals has said he will not support a proposed $2.8bn (£2.1bn) arms sale to Israel.

Gregory Meeks said he would not back the transfer of 2,000lb (900kg) bombs to Israel over concerns they might not be used in accordance with international law.

The New York congressman's objection follows reports that the US is planning to supply Israel with 40,000 of what Meeks called "some of the most destructive munitions in our arsenal".

But his objection is not enough to stop the sale - President Donald Trump's administration can sidestep Congress and press ahead anyway.

Meeks, a ranking member on the House of Representatives Foreign Affairs Committee, said in a statement he remained committed to Israel's security.

But he said that the deal "raises grave, unresolved concerns about how these munitions could be used in densely populated areas of Gaza and Lebanon".

He said it reflected Congress's "responsibility to ensure that US-funded weapons are used lawfully, responsibly, and with meaningful safeguards for human life".

The BBC has asked the Israeli Embassy for comment.

J Street, a liberal pro-Israel advocacy group, said in a statement to Israeli newspaper Haaretz: "You cannot rebuild Gaza with 2,000lb bombs."

Lawmakers are informed by the US state department about arms sales exceeding a set dollar amount, allowing them to place an informal hold on the deal.

But the president can go ahead with the deal if he declares that an emergency requires an immediate sale.

A veto-proof resolution passed jointly by two-thirds of the House and Senate would be required to block the weapons transfer.

Israel's use of General Dynamics-manufactured 2,000lb bombs in Gaza has drawn international anger owing to their devastating effects in densely populated civilian areas.

In 2024, then-President Joe Biden paused a shipment of the bombs to Israel - a move reversed when President Trump returned to office last year.

The supply of the weapons is reported to be under Foreign Military Financing, a programme funded by American taxpayers that provides billions of dollars each year for Israel and other allies to buy US-made weapons.

The US-Israel relationship still has substantial bipartisan backing, but support has been softening among Democrats.

In July, Republican lawmaker Thomas Massie forced a vote on a bill to cut $3.3bn in security aid to Israel and he received support from 103 Democrats in the chamber. He was the only Republican to support the amendment.

articles.title: Túnel entre Independência e Vargas tem interdição em Ribeirão  | G1
articles.standfirst: Local passará por serviços de manutenção na manhã desta quinta-feira (17). Orientação é usar rotas alternativas por vias como a Avenida Nove de Julho.
articles.summary: O túnel Independência-Presidente Vargas em Ribeirão Preto passa por manutenção nesta quinta-feira (17), com orientação para motoristas utilizarem rotas alternativas.
articles.body:
Túnel José Bonifácio tem quase 400 metros de extensão em Ribeirão Preto (SP) — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

O Túnel "José Bonifácio de Andrada e Silva" , que liga as avenidas Independência e Presidente Vargas, em Ribeirão Preto (SP), será interditado para manutenção na manhã desta quinta-feira (17).

Segundo a Prefeitura, o bloqueio ocorrerá a partir das 8h30 para sucção da água acumulada e outros serviços da Secretaria de Infraestrutura e Zeladoria com a Secretaria de Água e Esgoto (Saerp).

O local será sinalizado pela RP Mobi, e os motoristas serão orientadas a usar rotas alternativas como pela Avenida Nove de Julho e pelas ruas João Penteado e Altino Arantes.

A administração municipal não deu uma previsão de término da interdição, mas comunicou que o tráfego será liberado logo após a conclusão dos serviços de manutenção.

Uma das obras mais esperadas dos últimos anos em Ribeirão Preto, o túnel entre as avenidas Independência e Presidente Vargas foi inaugurado em 2023, após mais de três anos de espera por parte dos moradores e um atraso de um ano e meio na entrega, com relação ao prazo original.

Motoristas reclamam que, desde que foi entregue, o túnel tem sido constantemente interditado, principalmente depois que chove.

VÍDEOS: Tudo sobre Ribeirão Preto, Franca e região

articles.title: Reforma do Judiciário: Parlamentares propõem mandatos para o STF | G1
articles.standfirst: Propostas preveem mandato para ministros do STF, mudanças no sistema de indicação e novas regras para magistrados. Ao menos 30 projetos sobre o tema tramitam no Congresso.
articles.summary: Projetos de reforma do Judiciário no Congresso Nacional preveem mandatos fixos para ministros do STF e mudanças nos critérios de indicação à Corte.
articles.body:
Em meio à crise no Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ), parlamentares articulam no Congresso Nacional propostas para uma reforma do poder Judiciário. Ao menos 30 iniciativas sobre o tema tramitam nas duas casas.

A maior parte delas está concentrada em mudanças relacionadas ao STF, como a criação de mandatos para ministros, alterações no sistema de indicação e novos critérios para ocupar uma vaga na Corte.

Na semana passada, o deputado federal Reginaldo Lopes (PT-MG), apresentou uma proposta de emenda à Constituição (PEC) que prevê, entre outras medidas, mandato de dez anos e idade mínima de 50 anos para ministros da Corte.

O texto prevê mandato único e improrrogável de até dez anos para ministros e conselheiros de tribunais superiores, como o STF, e cortes de contas. O mandato começa na posse e termina no décimo aniversário da posse ou quando o magistrado completar 75 anos.

Além disso, estabelece a idade mínima de 50 anos e máxima de 70 anos para futuras nomeações nas Cortes superiores.

Nos próximos quatro anos, três ministros do Supremo Tribunal Federal irão atingir a idade de aposentadoria compulsória , são eles: Luiz Fux, Cármen Lúcia e Gilmar Mendes. Além dessas três vagas, há o posto aberto em decorrência da aposentadoria de Luís Roberto Barroso.

Com isso, o próximo presidente poderá escolher até quatro ministros no Supremo.

Na última semana, o deputado Danilo Forte (PP-CE) também apresentou uma proposta sobre o tema. Entre as principais mudanças estão a criação de mandato de oito anos para novos ministros do STF, a divisão das indicações à Corte entre Executivo, Legislativo e Judiciário e a adoção de novas regras de conduta e responsabilização para magistrados.

A PEC pretende tornar a indicação de ministros rotativa pelos Poderes Executivo, Legislativo e Judiciário.

A proposta também busca ampliar transparência da magistratura e estabelecer novos mecanismos de responsabilização. O texto também restringe decisões monocráticas.

Segundo o texto, a proposta preserva os mandatos dos atuais integrantes da Corte e determina que o modelo seja implementado gradualmente, à medida que ocorrerem vagas na Corte.

🔎 Os deputados ainda estão recolhendo assinaturas para protocolar as propostas. Para que uma PEC seja apresentada formalmente e passe a tramitar, são necessárias as assinaturas de pelo menos 171 dos 513 deputados.

Em outra frente, a Comissão de Direitos Humanos (CDH) aprovou nesta terça-feira (15) uma indicação da senadora Damares Alves (Republicanos-DF) para que a Comissão de Constituição e Justiça (CCJ) crie um grupo de trabalho responsável por reunir propostas de reforma do Judiciário que já estão em tramitação no Congresso.

A sugestão prevê que o colegiado consolide propostas de emenda à Constituição (PECs) e projetos de lei sobre o tema e apresente um texto unificado em até 60 dias. A indicação será encaminhada à CCJ, que decidirá se acolhe ou não a proposta.

A última reforma do Judiciário ocorreu em 2004 , após quase 13 anos de tramitação no Congresso.

A medida criou o Conselho Nacional de Justiça (CNJ) e o Conselho Nacional do Ministério Público (CNMP), além de promover mudanças em diversos dispositivos da Constituição relacionados ao funcionamento do sistema de Justiça.

O Supremo também discute o tema. O grupo criado pelo STF para discutir a reforma do Judiciário recebeu 87 propostas apresentadas por diversos órgãos e entidades da sociedade civil e que trazem pontos polêmicos, como adoção de mandato para ministros do STF, limitação de decisões individuais, além de novos mecanismos de controle e responsabilização.

A discussão sobre mudanças institucionais também inclui a elaboração de um código de ética, apontado como uma das prioridades do presidente da Corte, ministro Edson Fachin.

A estátua 'A Justiça', em frente ao prédio do STF e ao fundo Prédio do Congresso Nacional. — Foto: TON MOLINA/FOTOARENA/ESTADÃO CONTEÚDO

A crise na Corte se intensificou após o ministro André Mendonça levantar o sigilo de relatórios da Polícia Federal sobre as investigações do Banco Master.

Um dos documentos apontou 52 mensagens entre o banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro e o ministro Alexandre de Moraes , além de encontros presenciais entre os dois e de um contrato de R$ 130 milhões entre o banco e o escritório da mulher de Moraes, Viviane Barci de Moraes.

A divulgação dos documentos provocou um confronto entre Moraes e André Mendonça, relator das investigações do caso Master.

Moraes acusou o colega de fazer uma liberação "seletiva" dos autos e de omitir documentos. Mendonça negou e afirmou que manteve sob sigilo apenas informações necessárias para preservar investigações em andamento e dados de terceiros.

A disputa também envolveu o acesso às provas extraídas do celular de Vorcaro. Moraes, Cristiano Zanin e Gilmar Mendes pediram acesso integral ao material.

Após determinação de Zanin, a PF confirmou, na segunda-feira (14), ter entregue cópias do acervo digital aos três gabinetes . A PGR também se manifestou a favor da ampliação do acesso aos documentos.

Diante do conflito, o presidente do STF, Edson Fachin, decidiu separar os processos . O caso que envolve as mensagens entre Vorcaro e Moraes começou a ser analisado pelo Plenário nesta terça-feira (15).

A sessão foi marcada por embates entre os ministros até ser interrompida por um pedido de vista do ministro Flávio Dino. Com o pedido de vista, Dino tem até 90 dias para devolver o processo para análise . O prazo se encerra em dezembro deste ano.

Já as acusações de Moraes contra Mendonça ficaram para 23 de setembro.

articles.title: Gastos de campanha presidenciáveis 2026 somam R$ 151 milhões no TSE | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidatos apostam em serviços de marketing digital, viagens e impulsionamento de conteúdo. Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro, respectivamente, lideram total de despesas declaradas à justiça eleitoral.
articles.summary: Os gastos de campanha dos presidenciáveis em 2026 somam R$ 151 milhões, com Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro liderando investimentos em marketing digital, viagens e serviços jurídicos.
articles.body:
Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro, Augusto Cury, Ronaldo Caiado, Renan Santos e Romeu Zema — Foto: Globo

A 17 dias do primeiro turno, os principais candidatos à Presidência já gastaram R$ 151 milhões na campanha eleitoral, segundo dados do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) atualizados até esta quinta-feira (17). A votação será em 4 de outubro.

Lula (PT) concentra a maior fatia das despesas declaradas até agora: R$ 65 milhões . Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) vem logo atrás, com R$ 55 milhões . Depois aparecem Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), com R$ 24 milhões , e Romeu Zema (Novo), com R$ 4 milhões . Renan Santos (Missão) declarou R$ 1,2 milhão , enquanto Augusto Cury (Avante) informou gastos de R$ 265 mil .

🔎 Os dados são do DivulgaCand, plataforma do TSE, e fazem parte da prestação parcial de contas, que reúne as movimentações financeiras das campanhas entre 16 de agosto e 8 de setembro. O prazo para o envio dessas informações terminou em 13 de setembro. A prestação final deve ser apresentada até 30 dias após a eleição — ou após o segundo turno, para quem seguir na disputa. Candidatos eleitos que não prestarem contas não podem ser diplomados enquanto estiverem omissos.

📝 A cada eleição, o TSE estabelece um teto de gastos para cada cargo em disputa. Em 2026, os candidatos à Presidência podem gastar até R$ 88,9 milhões no primeiro turno e mais R$ 44,5 milhões no segundo. Quem chegar à etapa final da disputa poderá, portanto, desembolsar até R$ 133,4 milhões ao longo da campanha.

A disputa por atenção dos eleitores consome boa parte desses milhões. Entre as principais despesas dos candidatos estão publicidade, estratégia digital, impulsionamento de conteúdo nas redes sociais, viagens e serviços jurídicos.

Apesar da diferença de orçamento entre as campanhas, os gastos revelam estratégias parecidas. Comunicação digital, impulsionamento nas redes e serviços advocatícios aparecem nas contas de quase todos os presidenciáveis.

E a corrida pelo voto não ficou restrita às telas. Mesmo com o peso crescente na presença digital, a velha publicidade de rua segue firme: adesivos, santinhos e bandeiras continuam fazendo parte do arsenal das campanhas.

16.09.2026 – O presidente da República, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, participa de podcast, no Palácio da Alvorada, Brasília — Foto: Ricardo Stuckert

O presidente e candidato à reeleição declarou R$ 65 milhões em gastos de campanha até agora, o maior valor entre os presidenciáveis.

Quase metade desse total (47%) foi em um contrato de R$ 31 milhões com a agência Delta3 Comunicação para serviços “especializados de comunicação e marketing”, segundo o registro no Divulgacand.

A agência pertence ao publicitário baiano Raul Rabelo e ao diretor de cinema Francisco Mascarenhas Kertész, o Chico Kertész. Os dois foram sócios de Sidônio Palmeira, atual ministro da Secretaria de Comunicação Social e integrante da campanha presidencial de Lula, na M4 Comunicação e Propaganda, posteriormente rebatizada de Nordx Estratégia e Criatividade. Sidônio não integra mais o quadro societário da empresa.

Em seguida, há um registro de R$ 4,2 milhões para a empresa Log Produções & Filmes. Desse total, R$ 4,1 milhões foram para serviços técnicos e especializados, e R$ 120 mil para captação e transmissão ao vivo de eventos de promoção da candidatura.

A campanha também declarou R$ 2,7 milhões em publicidade impressa e adesivos. O valor foi destinado à NMC Gráfica por meio de 100 pagamentos para a produção de materiais como cartazes e adesivos.

Em estratégia digital, foram declarados R$ 2,5 milhões em impulsionamento de conteúdo no Facebook, divididos em 21 pagamentos. Embora as despesas sejam registradas em nome da plataforma, os anúncios também podem circular nos outros aplicativos da Meta, como o Instagram. A campanha declarou ainda R$ 100 mil em impulsionamento no Kwai.

Os serviços jurídicos somam outros R$ 4 milhões. O dinheiro foi distribuído entre cinco escritórios de advocacia. O maior valor, de R$ 1,5 milhão, foi destinado ao Ferraro e Novaes Advogados, de Ângelo Ferraro, coordenador jurídico da campanha. As outras firmas contratadas são:

Pellegrini & Sodre Sociedade de Advogados: R$ 800 mil;

Peccinin & Alessi Sociedade de Advogados: R$ 795 mil;

Lacombe e Neves da Silva Advogados Associados: R$ 702 mil;

Lula também destinou R$ 1,5 milhão à realização de pesquisas eleitorais internas, contratadas com a Oma Pesquisa, e R$ 1,2 milhão à Kaos Produz para produção e organização de eventos de campanha. Outros gastos com eventos incluem R$ 1 milhão na locação de equipamentos de iluminação, áudio e LED e R$ 905 mil com montagem, credenciamento e estrutura.

O candidato ainda distribuiu R$ 950 mil entre diferentes diretórios estaduais do Partido dos Trabalhadores. A divisão foi a seguinte:

Flávio Bolsonaro fez campanha nesta quarta-feira (9) em Juiz de Fora (MG), a cidade onde seu pai levou uma facada durante a campanha de 2018 — Foto: Pilar Olivares/Reuters

Flávio Bolsonaro declarou R$ 55 milhões em gastos de campanha até o momento. Entre as principais despesas estão estratégia eleitoral, produção de vídeos, comunicação, serviços jurídicos e fretamento de aeronaves, como mostrou o g1 .

A maior despesa, de R$ 13,1 milhões, foi com serviços de planejamento estratégico e marketing político. Outros R$ 5 milhões foram pagos à produtora Paranoá Digital por serviços descritos ao TSE como “planejamento digital”.

A campanha também declarou R$ 3,7 milhões para a criação de um canal no YouTube com programação 24 horas, dedicado à divulgação de propostas e notícias relacionadas à candidatura.

No impulsionamento de conteúdo nas redes sociais, os gastos declarados somam R$ 900 mil. Desse total, R$ 500 mil foram pagos à fintech DLocal, plataforma de processamento de pagamentos. A campanha explicou ao g1 que a empresa funciona como um “hub de pagamento” da Meta e que o valor corresponde à compra de créditos para anúncios em plataformas como Facebook e Instagram. Outros R$ 300 mil foram pagos diretamente ao Facebook e R$ 100 mil ao Kwai.

Na área de comunicação, a campanha de Flávio declarou R$ 3,6 milhões pagos à Algoritmo Dados Estratégia e Comunicação, agência de assessoria de imprensa fundada por Fábio Portela, ex-secretário especial de comunicação do prefeito de São Paulo, Ricardo Nunes. Uma segunda empresa de consultoria e assessoria de imprensa foi contratada por R$ 3,4 milhões.

Outros R$ 1,6 milhão foram destinados a um contrato de “assessoria executiva e coordenação de comitês e agendas estaduais”. A empresa de comunicação e marketing contratada foi fundada por Julio Martelo, ex-assessor político e relações públicas de integrantes da Assembleia Legislativa de São Paulo e da Câmara Municipal de Campinas.

Os serviços jurídicos também estão entre as despesas milionárias: R$ 3,1 milhões foram pagos ao escritório de Maria Claudia Bucchianeri, chefe jurídica da campanha e ex-ministra do TSE.

Com transporte aéreo, a campanha declarou gastos de R$ 2,2 milhões em fretamento de aeronaves com a Alljet Aviation, que atua nos segmentos de transporte executivo. Outros R$ 2 milhões foram gastos na produção de materiais de campanha, inclusive impressos, como cartazes, adesivos e bandeiras.

Augusto Cury em entrevista a podcast — Foto: Divulgação

Augusto Cury declarou até agora R$ 265 mil em gastos de campanha, a maior parte destinada ao impulsionamento de conteúdo nas redes sociais.

Dos valores informados, quase metade foi para o Facebook: R$ 120 mil, ou 45% do total. Foram três pagamentos: R$ 50 mil em 20 de agosto, R$ 50 mil em 29 de agosto e R$ 20 mil em 4 de setembro.

Outros R$ 36 mil foram para a prestação de serviços de assessoria logística e apoio operacional, e R$ 27 mil em 5 pagamentos para a produção de conteúdo audiovisual para a campanha. Cury ainda declarou R$ 18 mil gastos em consultoria de comunicação e marketing e R$ 24 mil, ao todo, em apoio às assessorias e aos demais setores da campanha.

As hospedagens em hotéis também compõem parte dos gastos declarados de Cury. Ao todo, foram R$ 16,2 mil em 8 locais diferentes. O valor inclui a hospedagem da equipe de suporte do candidato.

A prestação de contas inclui ainda R$ 958 em “lanche” para “participantes” de reuniões de trabalho, treinamento, capacitação e planejamento de ações da campanha.

Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) em sabatina nesta sexta-feira (4) ao Uol/Folha de São Paulo, nesta sexta-feira (4). — Foto: Reprodução/UOL

Ronaldo Caiado declarou R$ 24,2 milhões em gastos de campanha até agora. Desse total, R$ 20 milhões serão destinados a uma única empresa, responsável pelo marketing digital e pela produção de propaganda eleitoral para rádio e televisão.

Segundo a declaração ao TSE, a Épos Brasil receberá dois pagamentos de R$ 10 milhões cada pela prestação desses serviços, concentrando a maior parte das despesas declaradas pelo ex-governador de Goiás. A assessoria do candidato já disse ao g1 que o valor refere-se à contratação do serviço no decorrer da campanha, e que o valor ainda não foi pago em sua totalidade.

O segundo maior gasto declarado foi com a contratação de uma empresa de criação, planejamento e produção de conteúdo audiovisual por R$ 1 milhão.

Outra despesa de Caiado é de deslocamento em aeronaves particulares. Ao todo, ele contratou 5 empresas de táxi aéreo por R$ 1,1 milhão.

Os serviços jurídicos também aparecem na prestação parcial de contas. Caiado pagou R$ 500 mil ao escritório Malheiros, Penteado e Toledo por consultoria jurídica e R$ 425 mil ao escritório Boverio e Fernandes por serviços jurídicos eleitorais.

A campanha também destinou R$ 270 mil à Essent Inovação Contábil por serviços contábeis relacionados à prestação de contas eleitorais.

Nas redes sociais, Caiado direcionou R$ 246,7 mil para o impulsionamento de conteúdo no Facebook. Segundo a prestação de contas, o valor foi dividido em três pagamentos, realizados em 21 e 31 de agosto e 11 de setembro.

Renan Santos em entrevista à TV Jovem Pan nesta terça (8) — Foto: Reprodução/TV Jovem Pan

Renan Santos declarou R$ 1,2 milhão em gastos de campanha até agora, com a maior despesa concentrada na produção de materiais gráficos e publicidade impressa.

Desse total, R$ 292 mil foram pagos à WBL Gráfica & Editora, em sete pagamentos, para a produção de materiais como adesivos, bandeiras, “santões”, bandeiras para carros e adesivos para vidro traseiro. Outros R$ 89 mil foram destinados a uma segunda gráfica para a confecção de santinhos e adesivos.

A campanha também destinou R$ 100 mil à DLocal Brasil, ou seja, ao impulsionamento de conteúdos de campanha. Foram 3 pagamentos: R$ 50 mil e R$ 10 mil no dia 12 de agosto, e R$ 40 mil em 9 de setembro. Ele gastou mais R$ 90 mil com impulsionamento voltado ao próprio Facebook, totalizando R$ 190 mil para patrocinar suas postagens.

Outro gasto foi com serviços jurídicos: Santos pagou R$ 125 mil ao escritório Marella & Rollo.

O transporte também apareceu em diferentes contratações. Santos declarou R$ 85 mil na locação de um ônibus leito-cama com 22 poltronas, R$ 80 mil na compra de passagens aéreas para a equipe de campanha, por meio da Decolar.com, e R$ 12 mil no aluguel de carros para seu dia a dia.

Outra despesa foi com a taxa de administração do financiamento coletivo. A campanha pagou R$ 25 mil à plataforma Quero Apoiar. Segundo o ranking da própria empresa, Santos é o candidato que mais arrecadou por meio da plataforma neste ano: foram R$ 2,1 milhões de mais de 31 mil pessoas, até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Romeu Zema, candidato à Presidência da República pelo partido Novo — Foto: Rodilei Morais/Fotoarena/Estadão Conteúdo

Romeu Zema declarou R$ 4,1 milhões em gastos de campanha até agora, com boa parte das despesas concentrada em comunicação digital, produção de conteúdo e relacionamento com a imprensa.

O maior gasto declarado pelo ex-governador de Minas Gerais foi de R$ 930 mil em consultoria e produção de marketing digital. O valor foi dividido em três pagamentos: R$ 350 mil, R$ 180 mil e R$ 400 mil.

Zema também destinou R$ 450 mil a uma consultoria para coordenação da comunicação digital, tradicional e com a imprensa. Outros R$ 320 mil foram usados na produção e edição de conteúdos audiovisuais. Além disso, direcionou R$ 167 mil para a produção de adesivos e bottons.

A comunicação aparece ainda em uma série de despesas menores declaradas pela campanha:

R$ 72 mil para uma empresa de produção — R$ 47 mil para eventos e R$ 25 mil para a produção de “narrativas” para conteúdos audiovisuais, segundo a descrição apresentada pelo candidato;

R$ 61,5 mil para produção de conteúdos audiovisuais e apoio logístico às gravações;

R$ 60 mil para produção de jingles, vinhetas e slogans;

R$ 60 mil para a produção de conteúdo para mídias digitais;

R$ 55 mil em serviços de “planejamento”;

R$ 50 mil para edição de conteúdo, direção de fotografia e captações audiovisuais;

R$ 50 mil em serviços de assessoria de comunicação;

R$ 45 mil para a gestão e produção de conteúdo para plataformas;

R$ 44 mil em gestão de tráfego pago e impulsionamento;

R$ 40 mil em assessoria de comunicação institucional e relacionamento com veículos de imprensa.

Fora da área de comunicação, Zema priorizou seu deslocamento. Declarou R$ 155 mil em agenciamento de viagens, R$ 98,3 mil pelo aluguel de uma aeronave da Flapper Private Jets e R$ 79 mil na locação de veículos.

Também contratou o escritório Bessoni & Fortes advogados por R$ 300 mil, o escritório Santana Santos advocacia por R$ 100 mil, e o escritório Arnaldo Esteves Lima & Barbosa Moreira por R$ 70 mil.

articles.title: Campanha de Lula quer 'virar a página' de disputa no STF | G1
articles.summary: Campanha de Lula prioriza pautas sociais e tenta se afastar da crise no STF entre Moraes e Mendonça para conter o avanço eleitoral de Flávio Bolsonaro nas pesquisas.
articles.body:
Passada a sessão do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ) que discutiu o relatório da Polícia Federal (PF) que cita o ministro Alexandre de Moraes , que terminou sem um desfecho , integrantes da campanha do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) defendem "virar a página" sobre o assunto.

A avaliação é de que o tema favorece o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), candidato à Presdiência da República, e que é preciso mudar a pauta para problemas concretos das pessoas.

A principal estratégia da coordenação da campanha tem sido intensificar a comparação entre os governos de Lula e de Jair Bolsonaro (PL).

A última pesquisa Quaest que mostrou Flávio Bolsonaro numericamente à frente no segundo turno acendeu uma luz amarela no núcleo duro da campanha petista.

Nas últimas horas, as redes da campanha têm intensificado postagens reforçando a lembrança de crises agudas do governo Bolsonaro, como o desrespeito com pacientes de Covid-19, a fila para adquirir ossos por moradores com fome e ataques a mulheres.

Integrantes da campanha afirmam que o objetivo é desconstruir a família Bolsonaro e estimular o anti-bolsonarismo.

Os ministros do STF, Gilmar Mendes e Alexandre de Moraes, e o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva durante a solenidade — Foto: Marcelo Camargo/Agência Brasil

A conta é de que o aumento da rejeição de Flávio Bolsonaro entre eleitores independentes favoreceria a campanha de Lula.

Enquanto isso, o presidente tem tentado se descolar de Alexandre de Moares, enfatizando o tom adotado pela campanha de que "ninguém está acima da lei".

Em entrevista a um podcast nesta quarta (16) disse:

"Eu não era presidente quando o Alexandre de Moraes foi indicado para ministro da Suprema Corte", disse Lula.

Outros integrantes da campanha já têm elevado o tom.

"Reconheço, louvo e aplaudo os esforços do ministro Alexandre de Moraes para salvar a democracia. Mas era obrigação constitucional dele. Isso não gera salvo-conduto", afirma o coordenador do Grupo Prerrogativas e um dos coordenadores da campanha de Lula, Marco Aurélio de Carvalho.

O desafio é superar uma correlação entre Moraes e Lula. A campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro intensificou a associação entre ministro e candidato.

A estratégia deste campo político é tratar Lula e Moraes como duas faces da mesma moeda.

Integrantes do núcleo bolsonarista estão usando nas redes os nomes "Alexandre da Silva" e "Lula de Moraes" como forma de engajar a militância a associar ambos os personagens.

articles.title: VÍDEO: Posso levar cola para votar? | G1
articles.standfirst: A 'colinha eleitoral' é permitida na hora da votação, mas as informações precisam estar anotadas no papel. É proibido o uso de celular na cabine de votação.
articles.summary: A 'colinha eleitoral' é permitida na hora da votação, mas as informações precisam estar anotadas no papel. É proibido o uso de celular na cabine de votação.
articles.body:
O eleitor pode levar uma cola em papel para votar. Como são vários números para lembrar, é possível anotar os números dos candidatos e consultar o papel na cabine de votação.

É proibido o uso do celular na urna eletrônica , assim como tablets e outros aparelhos tecnológicos, como óculos inteligentes com câmeras. O eleitor pode usar o telefone para apresentar o e-Título antes de votar. Depois disso, porém, precisa deixar o aparelho no local indicado pelos mesários.

📍 Em uma série de 50 vídeos , o g1 explica os principais temas das eleições de 2026. Os conteúdos mostram como funcionam as pesquisas, explicam o papel dos cargos em disputa e o funcionamento do Congresso, e trazem orientações práticas para votar. A série também aborda o impacto das novas tecnologias na campanha, como inteligência artificial, deepfakes e influenciadores.

Para facilitar a organização, o g1 disponibilizou um modelo que pode ser impresso e preenchido com os números dos candidatos, já na ordem em que eles aparecem na urna.

Infográfico mostra a ordem de votação nas eleições de 2026 — Foto: Equipe de arte/g1

O primeiro turno das eleições será realizado em 4 de outubro de 2026 . O segundo turno está marcado para 25 de outubro de 2026 .

articles.title: Dem insurgent turns on the charm with party establishment as Schumer leaves bitter feud hanging
articles.summary: Abdul El-Sayed met with Chuck Schumer and Senate Democrats at DSCC headquarters in Washington, D.C., but few would say if primary wounds had healed.
articles.body: Michigan’s insurgent progressive Senate nominee ran as far as he could from Washington, D.C., but on Wednesday he traveled to the nation’s Capitol for a closed-door meeting with top Democratic brass as the race for power intensifies. Abdul El-Sayed met with top Senate Democrats just hundreds of yards away from Congress, where lawmakers and the wunderkind candidate huddled to discuss his campaign and how to keep Michigan blue. Many left boasting that the Wolverine State would not turn a shade of purple. But, few, including Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., would say whether the fences broken during El-Sayed’s primary fight had been mended. SCHUMER DUCKS QUESTION ON CAMPAIGNING WITH SOCIALIST CANDIDATE WHO REFUSES TO BACK HIM AS LEADER "Look, we have to win Michigan and we had a great and friendly meeting," Schumer said when asked by Fox News Digital if he and El-Sayed had moved on from their differences. Still, El-Sayed held court with Democratic brass for hours at the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee’s (DSCC) headquarters in Washington, where a steady flow of lawmakers — both allies and skeptics of his Senate bid — milled in and out of the building throughout the day. Schumer and Democrats are confident and determined that they can flip the Senate, which Republicans hold at a 53 to 47 margin. Losing Michigan to the GOP and former Rep. Mike Rogers would serve a mortal blow to that push. "He’s gonna win," Sen. Kirstin Gillibrand, D-N.Y., who is also the DSCC chair, said. The key mission for Democrats is getting independents and Republicans on the fence. But few, including Schumer, said that they would actually hit the campaign trail with El-Sayed. It all comes after El-Sayed and Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., locked horns in one of the most bitter Democratic primary fights of this cycle that pitted the Democratic old-guard versus a progressive movement gaining steam across the country. SEE IT: DEM SENATORS RALLY BEHIND EL-SAYED BUT DUCK QUESTIONS ON PROGRESSIVE AGENDA Sen. Chris Murphy, D-Conn., who initially endorsed Michigan state Sen. Mallory McMorrow before she dropped out, told Fox News Digital that, "obviously, primaries can get really hot, and the Michigan primary got hot." "This is what you do after a primary is you try to unite the party and then you do the work to reach out and cross over to independent voters and Republican voters," Murphy said. "So I don't think anybody should be surprised that he's trying to build bridges after a heated primary. That's what good candidates, that's what winning candidates do." Another McMorrow backer, Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., painted a rosy picture of the closed-door session, and noted that it was "hard to hear in there because so many people were talking and laughing and wanted to hear about the campaign." "He makes good connections because it's a lot of people in there who are talking about what can we do next? What can we do to lower costs for families? What can we do to make this government work better for working people? So it was a very enthusiastic, very cheerful group of people," she said. Retiring Sen. Gary Peters, D-Mich., whose seat El-Sayed is gunning for, initially endorsed Stevens. Now, he’s shifting gears. DEMS' LEFTWARD LURCH GETS LEGS AS EL-SAYED'S MICHIGAN SENATE VICTORY SPARKS PARTY DEBATE "I'm endorsing him, and he's been getting support across the board in Michigan. The Democrats are coming together," Peters said in response to a question about whether the Democratic establishment was uniting behind El-Sayed. "We understand how important this election is." Others were more keen to lend an assist to El-Sayed, including Murphy and Sen. Mark Kelly, D-Ariz., who said, "I’m gonna be in Michigan here in a couple of weeks." Sen. Ed Markey, D-Mass., who is running for re-election in deep blue Massachusetts, said that Democrats’ strategy heading into the final stretch was pitching an affordability agenda, and that El-Sayed "is the answer." "I'm helping him. I think we're all gonna help," Markey said when asked if he would fundraise with El-Sayed. The specter of El-Sayed’s relationship with controversial Twitch streamer Hasan Piker, who helped to amplify his campaign in the primary battle, wasn’t something that Democrats focused on during their huddle. "Hasan what?," Senate Minority Whip Dick Durbin, D-N.Y., told Fox News Digital when asked if he came up during the meeting. "I don’t even know who that is." When asked if Piker came up, or if Democrats encouraged El-Sayed to further distance himself from him, Sen. Andy Kim, D-N.J., said, "Not in terms of the conversation. Like I said, I was just trying to get to know him." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP After initially dodging Fox News Digital’s question on whether he would campaign with Piker, El-Sayed later told reporters that, "This conversation is so far removed from what people are talking about." "Everyday, in Michigan, people sit at their kitchen tables and ask ‘how am I going to make this work next month?’ That’s not a middle, right, left issue, that’s a basic affordability issue," El-Sayed said. But when further pressed, he countered that Michigan voters "really don’t care about that." "They really don't," El-Sayed said.

articles.title: Trump says Kennedy Center could be 'ripped down' if he doesn't get 'recognition'
articles.summary: A federal judge blocked Trump's name from being added to the building.
articles.body:
President Donald Trump said on Wednesday the Kennedy Center could "close" or be "ripped down" if his administration doesn't receive recognition on the performing arts center as tensions over his name being removed mount.

"I think that the Trump administration should certainly have recognition. Because frankly, if we don't do that, it's going to close. It'll end up being ripped down," the president told reporters on the tarmac in North Carolina.

Trump claimed that the Kennedy Center was a "mess" without his intervention and "has lost 10s of millions of dollars, even hundreds of millions of dollars," comparing it to New York's Carnegie Hall.

The president's comments come after a federal judge on Tuesday blocked the performing arts center's board from adding a tribute to Trump on the building or site. He responded by saying he wouldn't spend congressionally approved funding for the center's renovation unless the building also bears his name.

Congress last year appropriated $257 million for the renovation.

About an hour after the judge's ruling Tuesday, the board, which is controlled by Trump appointees, voted to close the center immediately for renovations, citing safety concerns after a piece of plaster from the ceiling of the grand foyer fell during a heavy rainstorm earlier this month.

On Tuesday, Rep. Joyce Beatty, D-Ohio, said Trump "threw a tantrum because he lost in court" when discussing the Kennedy Center meeting.

"He wasn't pleased with it. He was very explicit with his words, and I responded equally as explicit. He is in contempt of court for what he's doing now in trying to just simply go over and close the Kennedy Center and to have people leave the center," Beatty told reporters on the House steps Tuesday night.

Beatty said "there was a heated debate" during the meeting.

On Wednesday, fencing was seen being installed around the main building's entrance.
authors: KAREN TRAVERS, MICHELLE STODDART and DEVIN GARBITT

articles.title: Trump credits Whatley for GOP’s past ‘record setting’ election wins in NC rally
articles.summary: President Trump made his first campaign stop in North Carolina Wednesday since last week’s Republican National Committee (RNC) Midterm Convention, rallying for Senate candidate Michael Whatley as Republicans hope to keep the Tar Heel State’s seat red this November. Trump claimed the battleground state during his three presidential runs. He told the Gastonia, North Carolina,…
articles.body:
President Trump made his first campaign stop in North Carolina Wednesday since last week’s Republican National Committee (RNC) Midterm Convention, rallying for Senate candidate Michael Whatley as Republicans hope to keep the Tar Heel State’s seat red this November.

Trump claimed the battleground state during his three presidential runs. He told the Gastonia, North Carolina, crowd Wednesday that Whatley — who formerly co-chaired the RNC alongside his daughter-in-law, Lara Trump — helped him secure these wins.

“We won those record-setting victories with the help of a man named Michael Whatley,” Trump said. “He was incredible.”

The president went on to praise the GOP candidate for his time chairing the RNC with his daughter-in-law. In 2025, Trump gave Whatley his blessing to pursue the North Carolina Senate seat, which Lara Trump briefly pursued before dropping her bid.

“Nobody better in the whole country. I had my choice of the whole country. I chose Michael Whatley,” Trump said.

The stop in North Carolina came as recent polls showed Whatley trailing his Democratic opponent, former North Carolina Gov. Roy Cooper (D) — who was in office from 2017 to 2014.

In an Elon University poll published Monday, 49 percent of likely voters said they backed Cooper, while 38 percent said they supported Whatley. Another 14 percent said they were undecided or planned to vote for someone else.

Whatley for his part spoke about his relationship with Trump, going back to 2015 when he said he was asked to “help a businessman run for president.”

“Here we are, 11 years later, and every single day, Donald Trump is fighting to make America great,” the candidate said. “And I am still with that guy, and I’m excited about running for Senate because I want every North Carolina family to make more money, to keep more money.”

Trump attacked Cooper during his Wednesday remarks, calling the former governor part of the “radical left” and a “murderer protector.” He claimed crime ticked up in the state under Cooper’s leadership and accused him of doing “nothing” for Hurricane Helene victims in 2024.

The president repeated a line he used at the midterm convention and throughout the 2026 election cycle, urging voters to pretend he’s on the November ballot.

“But at this election, I’m asking you to pretend I’m on the ballot just one more time,” he said. “Because when I’m on the ticket, I’m not bragging, but when I’m on the ticket, Republicans have always done really well.”

“Everybody gets elected when I’m on,” he continued. “But I just want you to go out and pretend I’m on the ticket because essentially I am.”

This election comes amid a tough political landscape, with the GOP grappling with historical headwinds, sinking approval ratings and fallout from the war in Iran.

Trump reiterated the Iran war is “going to end soon” and called the increased gas prices amid the conflict a “very inexpensive price to pay for what we’ve done.”

“It’s going to be a really good conclusion,” the president said, adding that it could be “after the election, but maybe not.”

Trump also reiterated an announcement he made at last week’s convention that American adults will receive $5,000 checks if the Republicans win the midterm election — the logistics of which since coming under scrutiny.

“And remember, if the Republicans win the House and Senate, I will issue what we will all call from now on the Trump dividend to every adult in America,” he said. “We’ll get $5,000, and you’ll get it because we’re taking in so much money, and we can do it.”

The president also told the Gastonia crowd that his Big, Beautiful Bill tax cuts — including no tax on tips, Social Security and overtime — will be made permanent.

articles.title: Democrat candidate seen sobbing, praying in patrol car after DUI arrest: Video
articles.summary: Police video shows Washington state Democrat Krista Perez admitting to drinking wine and begging to go home during her Tacoma DUI arrest in August.
articles.body: Washington state Democrat Krista Perez, who is running for a state House seat, was seen on police video admitting to drinking wine, declining field sobriety tests and begging to go home before praying and crying in the back of a patrol car after her DUI arrest. Perez finished first in last month's primary in the 29th Legislative District, Position 1, and will face incumbent state Rep. Melanie Morgan, also a Democrat, in November, as the top two candidates advance to the general. Tacoma Police said Perez's 2019 Chevrolet Silverado allegedly struck a parked car on South G Street shortly after midnight on August 11, setting off a chain reaction that damaged five vehicles, according to The Jason Rantz Show on Seattle Red. Prosecutors charged her with DUI, with a refusal enhancement in connection with the collision and a later encounter with police. MASSACHUSETTS DEMOCRATIC PARTY CHAIRMAN ADMITS TO SUFFICIENT FACTS IN JUNE DRUNKEN DRIVING CASE Body camera footage shows police questioning Perez after the crash and her subsequent arrest, while footage from the backseat of the patrol car shows her praying and sobbing, according to video obtained by The Jason Rantz Show on Seattle Red. After police arrive at the scene, Perez told an officer she did not understand what was going on and claims she was not involved in an accident, the footage shows. "Did you get into an accident here?" the officer asks. "I did not," Perez responded. The officer then asked what happened. "I don’t know. I’ve never been in an accident before," she replied. She also said she switched insurers just weeks before the incident when asked for her documents. She was able to tell the officer the name of the insurance company. Perez told the officer she was driving from a friend’s business on Tacoma Avenue South when the collision happened. "Did you have anything to drink tonight?" the officer asked. "I just had some wine while I was there," Perez replied. Asked how much wine she had, Perez said she had one glass. When the officer asked how big the glass was, she told him, "I think you might need to contact the business." The officer then asked her to rate her sobriety on a scale of zero to 10, with zero being completely sober. She first told the officer that she wants to go home. But when asked a second time, she rated herself a four. The officer then asked her to take standardized field sobriety tests but stated multiple times that the tests are optional. "So it’s a series of tests that I take you through to make sure to see if you’re impaired by alcohol, or you’re not. Are you okay with doing that? It’s totally voluntary," he said. Perez declined the tests, kept saying she wanted to go home and repeatedly said that she was "confused." "Not right now. I’d like to go home first," she said. "You’re not going to go home first. I’m going to tell you that right now, okay? So your options between the test, yes or no, that’s going to be determined tonight, right now, not when you go home. So would you like to take these tests or no?" the officer asked. Perez responded by asking if she was allowed to decline the tests. "You do have a choice. You can either say yes, or you can say no. They’re totally voluntary tests," the officer answered. "Yeah, I would like to go home first," she replied. The officer asked whether her answer meant she was declining the tests, and she said yes. She was then told she was under arrest for DUI and to put her hands behind her back. "Hold on. Hold on. One second. Hold on," she said. Perez repeatedly told the officer that she did "not know what any of this means." He told her it means she is under arrest for DUI. Under Washington state law, roadside sobriety tests are not required and declining them is separate from the refusal enhancement prosecutors allege in Perez's case. According to an arrest report cited by The Jason Rantz Show on Seattle Red, the enhancement stems from what occurred later at Tacoma Police headquarters, where police said she did not provide a usable breath sample after three attempts before the machine timed out. BODYCAM SHOWS TONY ROMO ARGUING WITH OFFICER BEFORE REFUSING BREATH TEST DURING DUI ARREST CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Inside the patrol car, she can be seen in the footage sobbing, praying and asking God to help her, with her crying lasting several minutes. "Help me, God. Help me. Help me. Holy Spirit, help me, God," she said. State law does not prohibit someone with a DUI charge from serving in the legislature. Other Democrat lawmakers have kept their seats after an alcohol-related incident, including House Majority Leader Joe Fitzgibbon, who apologized after acknowledging he drank alcohol before a House Appropriations Committee hearing in February. "I made a poor choice last night by drinking alcohol before we had finished our work for the day. I am disappointed in myself and take responsibility for that poor choice. It won’t happen again, and I’m committed to completing my work this session without alcohol," Fitzgibbon said in a statement at the time to The Jason Rantz Show on Seattle Red.

articles.title: Rogers says he ‘never agreed’ to El-Sayed debate: It would’ve been ‘2-on-1’
articles.summary: Rep. Mike Rogers (R) said he “never agreed” to Tuesday’s televised debate with his Michigan Senate opponent, Democrat Abdul El-Sayed — who spoke for an hour next to an empty podium on a Fox 2 Detroit hours after the Republican announced he wouldn’t attend. Rogers reiterated to CBS News Detroit’s Heath Kalb that the moderator’s…
articles.body:
Rep. Mike Rogers (R) said he “never agreed” to Tuesday’s televised debate with his Michigan Senate opponent, Democrat Abdul El-Sayed — who spoke for an hour next to an empty podium on a Fox 2 Detroit hours after the Republican announced he wouldn’t attend.

Rogers reiterated to CBS News Detroit’s Heath Kalb that the moderator’s alleged “favoritism” led him to skip the event, saying it would’ve been a “two-on-one fight” as opposed to a debate.

“Well, first of all, it’s not a debate. It’s a town hall. We never agreed to it. And the one thing that’s been consistent is [Fox 2 Detroit anchor] Roop Raj has picked his candidate. We saw it in the debate between Abdul and Haley Stevens,” the candidate said, referring to El-Sayed’s opponent in Michigan’s Democratic primary.

He added, “You have someone who’s already picked their candidate, you can’t have a 2-on-1 event in a TV studio. I’ve really never quite seen anything like this in the media. I think it’s highly unprofessional.”

When asked about critics suggesting Rogers was unwilling to engage in a discussion with El-Sayed, the GOP candidate pointed out that the pair have two televised debates scheduled for October.

The representative also swiped at Raj for being “an impartial person,” saying the journalist should not have moderated the event “where he’s this invested in a particular candidate.”

“But you can’t have a media outlet set a date and say, ‘This is a debate and you must be here or we’re going to put an open podium on here.’ That’s highly unprofessional,” Rogers told Kalb.

Raj has defended himself against Rogers’ claims of favoritism, saying on Fox 2’s “Good Day Detroit” that the campaign did not want to do the debate “for whatever reason.” The anchor admitted he once called El-Sayed “brilliant” because of his background as a Rhodes Scholar before saying that he looks at both candidates as “tremendous political athletes.”

He wrote in an op-ed for The Detroit Free Press before the debate imploring Rogers to take part.

“They cited clips from various shows I’ve hosted to assert bias,” he wrote. “Our nightly political show has had moments of praise and criticism for Rogers and El Sayed. This is not personal. I have interviewed Rogers multiple times on TV, and on stage at a forum when he ran against now-U.S. Sen. Elissa Slotkin. There was no issue then. We have no issue now.”

After the debate, El-Sayed quipped that “ the elephant was not in the room ” of the debate, referring to Rogers’ absence.

“It’s wild to me that this guy is more interested in going to speak for what? Six minutes and 48 seconds in Dallas than he is to have 60 minutes with Michiganders here in Detroit,” El-Sayed said, referring to Rogers’s remarks at last week’s Republican National Committee midterm convention. “But it tells you who he is, he’s a coward.”

The Hill’s polling partner Decision Desk HQ gives El-Sayed a 66 percent chance of winning the race to succeed outgoing Sen. Gary Peters (D-Mich.) as of Wednesday night.

articles.title: Macklemore, Ed Sheeran ask Robert Kraft to donate to Palestinian humanitarian aid
articles.summary: New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft said Ed Sheeran asked him to match a $2 million donation to “aid in the region” after Macklemore — who was ousted from the pop star’s tour for promoting “Free Palestine” messaging — similarly urged him to donate. Kraft said in a Wednesday statement that, before Macklemore challenged the…
articles.body:
New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft said Ed Sheeran asked him to match a $2 million donation to “aid in the region” after Macklemore — who was ousted from the pop star’s tour for promoting “Free Palestine” messaging — similarly urged him to donate.

Kraft said in a Wednesday statement that, before Macklemore challenged the businessman to match his own $1 million donation to humanitarian aid in Gaza, Sheeran had made a $2 million contribution. According to the Patriots owner, the singer then asked him to match the $2 million he pledged.

“Ed now plans to reach out to other venue owners and our goal is to continue to work together to build bridges,” Kraft said in his statement, posted to the social media accounts of the Patriots’ Gillette Stadium.

“In addition, I’d like the people who are speaking in support of the Palestinian people to know that for decades, I have supported efforts to create opportunity for Palestinians and have brought young Palestinians and Israelis together to build businesses, create jobs and forge relationships,” he added.

As of Wednesday night, Sheeran has not confirmed his donation, nor has Kraft elaborated on to which humanitarian organizations the money was directed.

Macklemore said on Monday that Sheeran “and his team have made the decision to remove me from The Loop tour” — which included performing at Gillette later this month — after a phone call between the pop star and Kraft, a vocal supporter of Israel.

Macklemore wrote on Instagram Wednesday that he would donate $1 million of his net earnings from The Loop Tour to six organizations working to directly provide Palestinians with aid. He invited Kraft to do the same.

Following Macklemore’s ouster, Sheeran has faced backlash online as several other artists pulled out of the tour . The departures of Billish Eilish’s brother and music collaborator Finneas, Danish band Lukas Graham, Irish band Beoga and Aaron Rowe left the tour with no supporting acts.

Children’s YouTuber Ms. Rachel, another pro-Palestinian activist, accused Sheeran of making a political statement to his fans by performing to support Ukraine “but [considering] Palestine too dangerous and political” to back.

Macklemore has shown support for Palestinians during Israel’s nearly three-year war in Gaza, which began when militant group Hamas waged an attack on Israeli soil on Oct. 7, 2023. He also publicly backed students who protested the U.S.’s support for Israel throughout the conflict.

The rapper released “Hind’s Hall” in 2024, a song referencing the name that pro-Palestinian protesters gave a campus building at Columbia University — naming it after 5-year-old Hind Rajab after she and her family were killed in an Israeli attack in Gaza.

Kraft has donated to several Jewish and Israeli causes, formed the Foundation to Combat Antisemitism in 2019 in response to rising antisemitism in the U.S. and funded the campaign “Stand Up to Jewish Hate.” The Foundation to Combat Antisemitism became the Blue Square Alliance Against Hate in 2025.

In 2019, Kraft received the $1 million Genesis Prize, an annual award referred to as the “Jewish Nobel Prize,” for his support for Israel. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said during the award ceremony that “Israel does not have a more loyal friend than Robert Kraft.”

Former Vice President Kamala Harris will campaign for Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed (D) at a campaign event next week, according to multiple reports.

Harris will join El-Sayed, a doctor and former head of health departments in Detroit and Wayne County, at a roundtable focused on Black maternal health on Tuesday, The Associated Press reported Wednesday.

“Vice President Harris looks forward to returning to Michigan to help turn out the vote in this critical state,” Harris spokesperson Eduardo Negrón told the outlet. “It is critical we flip the Senate so we can bring down prices and stand up to Donald Trump’s corruption.”

The Hill has reached out to Harris’ team for comment.

El-Sayed told Politico on Wednesday that he looks forward to her arrival in Michigan, saying people in communities like Detroit “look up to [her] as an inspirational leader.” The candidate noted Black maternal health is an issue both he and Harris have been “a leader on.”

“I’m grateful that she’s coming in and having conversations about what it takes to get the turnout up, so that we can get on to working on some of these issues in the U.S. Senate,” he added.

Harris endorsed El-Sayed in his campaign against Rep. Mike Rogers (R-Mich.) in August, the latest of several establishment Democrats to announce their support for the populist candidate.

“While Michiganders struggle to afford everyday essentials — housing, gas, groceries, health care, and child care — Trump and Republicans in Congress are giving away $1 trillion in tax breaks to the wealthy and powerful,” Harris said in her endorsement.

“Abdul knows that we need bold solutions to the crises facing America’s working families, and he is ready to take on this fight. I proudly stand with him to ensure we win a Democratic Senate majority in November,” she added

The event comes one week after Rogers declined to participate in a debate with El-Sayed , hosted by Fox 2 Detroit on Tuesday. Rogers accused the moderator, Roop Raj, of showing bias toward El-Sayed — a claim that Raj has denied.

The Republican candidate said he “ never agreed ” to a debate. El-Sayed spoke next to an empty podium for the hour-long debate.

Harris has given support to several campaigns this election cycle amid speculation that she could run again for president in 2028 — after her 2024 loss to Trump. Though several Democratic candidates have moved away from the former vice president in an effort to distinguish themselves from the public’s perception of her time in office.

Were she to make a third bid for the presidency, California Gov. Gavin Newsom (D) — another potential 2028 Democratic presidential contender — said he would not pursue the position . The two worked together as elected officials in San Francisco, when he was the city’s mayor and Harris it’s district attorney.

“I know her base of supporters. I know her friends,” Newsom told CNN’s Jake Tapper while fly fishing in Montana. “The [Venn] diagram on that is just pure crossover. I wouldn’t do that to people.”
